title: Can a local GPT identify a sound without seeing its source?
model: gpt-6.1-terra via signed-in Codex CLI, low reasoning effort

method.clotho: 24 full, anonymous, audio-only recordings in Clotho v2.1 evaluation and Clotho-AQA test. Of 99 candidates outside a previous panel, take SHA-256 order of reel-causal-audio-v1/ + filename, skip previously published files, reference bank IDs and duplicate uploaders. Five human captions and four binary questions with three individual votes per recording. Evaluation uploaders and files are distinct within this panel. Model pretraining overlap is unknown.
method.delivery: MCP --tracks sound --image-client, view with continuous_seconds=8 and native_audio=false. The GPT receives compact reports and the recorded-channel spectrograms from the whole clip. No video frames, original filename, human descriptions or answer key. Both arms use local audio helpers including CoNeTTE, with the optional 30B waveform reader disabled. The GPT reader runs in a fresh session per recording and task. Each task uses one response per condition. Identical captures reuse their already blind response. For final capture, replayed the changed source reader on released PCM and replaced its field in the captured reports. Two complete real MCP recaptures reproduced all report fields and spectrograms.
method.caption_prompt: Describe what you heard in the recording in one or two short English sentences for someone who could not hear it. Include the most distinctive sounds and how they change. Identify sources only as precisely as the sound supports. Do not discuss the tools or repeat the question.
method.caption_score: Pinned all-MiniLM-L6-v2 as in examples/check_first_impressions.py. In each of five leave-one-human-out folds compare the reader (or held-out human) to the other four matching captions and the mean for each of the 23 other clips. Mean matching minus other cosine divided by the held-out human gap. Per-clip arrays contain matching cosine, other cosine, and top-one retrieval credit. The 95% interval resamples 24 recordings 10,000 times. It conditions on these captions, recordings and replies.
method.qa: Questions are fixed before model inference. Yes or no scores one per matching human vote. Unknown scores zero. Each human-human unordered pair counts once. The comparison with a different recording rotates audio by seven clips while keeping the same questions. Paired change intervals resample entire recordings 20,000 times.
method.foreground: FSD50K (Fonseca et al., CC BY 4.0), CC0 source originals. Four-second mono 24 kHz colored-noise and hum bed plus an energy-selected 0.5–1.6 s excerpt (shorter for short originals) at -3, 3, 9 or 15 dB. Exact recipe is in examples/check_focused_listening.py. Offsets and ranges in confirmation rows use 24 kHz samples. Human label applies to the source recording and can be ambiguous in the mixture. No known source or event boundary is passed to either reader.
method.development: 64 development mixtures. An initial PE-only focused rule (reference cosine >=0.65) on 128 further clips raised correct names from 12 to 13 and unmatched names from 6 to 10. Rejected. Calibrated the final PE text + reference audio + CLAP text check on the 64 development mixtures. Before confirmation, froze raw channel, top three in each ranking, rank product margin above 8, minimum scores 0.10/0.55/0.25. A matching broad label can be refined without CLAP. No class-specific thresholds.
method.confirmation: 128 other FSD50K evaluation recordings, distinct uploaders from the first 192 and from each other. At most three per class, no recording ID in the reference bank. Same final production SourceReader for all 128 mixtures and 128 matching background-only controls. The wide window gives the baseline name. Count each distinct claimed name per clip once. A clip may have both a hit and an unmatched name. Timing compares automatic excerpt versus known insertion using intersection over union, zero when no excerpt was picked.
method.gpt_sources: 48 fixed hash-selected foreground cases and 12 different beds from the first 128-case panel, chosen without model predictions. Each GPT receives the exact 4 s MCP listen report (describe=false, source_examples=true) and spectrogram. No choices. A separate blind gpt-6.1-terra grader rated unique answer/target pairs in hash order, without version labels. Compatible is reported separately. These are different recordings from the fresh confirmation set.
method.source_prompt: What made the brief foreground sound in this recording? Name the most specific sound source or sound action you can support in a few English words. If the source cannot be identified or only background is audible, answer unknown. Answer only with that name or unknown.
method.grading: Grade how well a blind listener named the inserted foreground source. The target is the human leaf label on the source recording. Exact = the same source/action or an ordinary synonym. Compatible = correct family, or an unverified more specific subtype. Wrong = different source/action. Unknown = explicit unidentified or no foreground answer. For null target (background only), use unknown for no foreground, wrong for an asserted new foreground; a generic description of the steady bed without a claimed new sound is unknown. Extra invented details must not promote compatible to exact. Return JSON {"items":[{"id":0,"grade":"exact|compatible|wrong|unknown"},...]} with all IDs.
method.field: Ten original TUT Sound Events 2016 evaluation field recordings. First recorded channel. Use up to eight hash-selected non-overlapping 4 s windows per recording with a directly mapped human event 0.15–2.5 s completely inside. 51 eligible windows. An unmatched name need not be absent from the real scene. For oracle_matched, give the original wide reader samples from one annotated event and compare against that event only. Natural field rows omit source annotations and waveform.
method.door: Same door film and 8.5 s cutoff. A contains the metallic cue, B has the bed alone, C shares A’s prefix and differs afterwards. Silent-track and picture-only controls. A/C compact reports and image bytes were hashed in streaming order. MCP rejected replay extending to 8.6 s for all cases with sound.

source_reader_time.hardware: Apple M4 Pro, 64 GiB, local cached weights
source_reader_time.method: Two successive isolated SourceReader runs on the same first 25 confirmation mixtures, before then after. Time includes IPC and waveform encoding, excludes GPT, playback, captions and other helpers. The first recording warms the process and is excluded from the median. One pass per condition.
